content:
Sergio Costa: Need sign-off on cache hit-rate regression alerts before we wire them into the new dashboards. Two open questions:
1) what thresholds = “regression” vs just traffic mix changing?
2) what should page vs ticket (noise budget)?

I’m proposing burn-rate style on `cache_hit_rate` + `cacheable_prompt_ratio` as a sanity check. Want input from oncall folks.

Sean Gallagher: +1 to burn-rate, but hit-rate is *super* sensitive to route mix / model version rollouts. If we page for every dip we’ll hate our lives.

What’s the unit we’re alerting on? Global? per-region? per-route?

Sergio Costa: draft was:
- scope: by region + deployment_mode first (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- primary signal: v2 `prefix_cache.hit_rate` (lookups weighted by tokens)
- secondary: `prefix_cache.saved_prefill_ms` and `prefix_cache.hit_bytes`
- guardrail: only evaluate when `cacheable_prompt_ratio >= 0.15` and `requests >= N`

Pages if burn rate > 2x for 30m AND > 1x for 6h (classic multiwindow) where burn rate is relative drop from baseline.

Rafael Mendes: “relative drop from baseline” is the hard part. What baseline? last 7d same hour? last 1h moving avg? We need something that doesn’t freak out during normal customer deploys.

Also: what are we calling regression? e.g. 45% -> 35% could be “all new prompts” not a bug.

Logan Wright: reminder: v2 hit-rate is defined as `hit_tokens / (hit_tokens + miss_tokens)` at lookup time, *not* per-request outcome. So it’s already traffic-weighted, but still mix-sensitive.

Mix changes we can detect via tags: `route_id`, `model_family`, `model_version`, `tenant_tier` (but we can’t alert on all of them without cardinality pain).

Allison Grant: SRE stance: page only on platform regression (pipeline/runtime/gateway). Customer behavior changes should be tickets/triage.

So we need a gating rule to distinguish platform-wide drop vs a single high-volume route shifting.

Mei Lin: can we use “top routes contribution” check? If global drops but 80% of delta is from one route’s traffic mix changing, don’t page.

Nadia Rahman: we can compute a lightweight “concentration” metric in the query:
- look at top 5 routes by request volume, compare their hit-rate deltas.
- if >= 3 routes across >= 2 tenants show similar drop, more likely platform.

But we should keep it simple for v1 alerting.

Sean Gallagher: +1 keep it simple. For paging, I want:
- only Hosted + Dedicated first (Private is too heterogeneous)
- region-level, not per-route
- require impact signal: `saved_prefill_ms` drops too (or prefill latency increases)

Because hit-rate can drop but if saved prefill doesn’t, it’s probably measurement weirdness.

Caleb Johnson: from ingestion side: we’ve seen sampling changes look like regressions. If the pipeline drops cache events due to cardinality guardrails, hit-rate can swing. We should include data quality checks.

We have a draft runbook for “missing/incorrect cache metrics” that covers sampling/tag explosion symptoms: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPLAT/cache-telemetry-data-quality-runbook

Rafael Mendes: yeah, oncall wants that runbook linked directly in the alert.

Also define explicitly what is NOT a regression:
- traffic moving to a new model version (expected miss spike)
- sudden increase in unique prompt prefixes (cacheable_prompt_ratio unchanged but hit-rate down)
- new tenant onboarded with cold cache

Sergio Costa: ok. Here’s an updated proposal based on this thread:

Paging alert: “Cache hit-rate platform regression (region, mode)”
- dimensions: `region`, `deployment_mode` (Hosted, Dedicated)
- evaluation window: 30m / 6h multiwindow
- condition A: `prefix_cache.hit_rate` drops by >= 20% relative (e.g. 0.40 -> 0.32) AND absolute drop >= 0.05
- condition B (impact): either `prefix_cache.saved_prefill_ms` drops by >= 15% OR `prefill_latency_p95` increases by >= 10%
- condition C (volume): `requests >= 2k` and `cacheable_prompt_ratio >= 0.15`
- suppression: during known rollout windows (feature flag ramp) + if telemetry ingestion error rate is elevated

Non-paging: ticket alert per-route (top offenders) into #eng-sre triage channel.

Sean Gallagher: That’s closer. I’d still tighten it: require *two* regions if Hosted (us-east + eu-west) to page, otherwise file a ticket. Single-region drops are often a capacity/routing thing that resolves.

Rafael Mendes: agree. If it’s only one region, page the region oncall only if it correlates w elevated 5xx or latency SLO burn.

Allison Grant: also include a “change detection” note in the alert text:
- check if `model_version` mix changed
- check if `cacheable_prompt_ratio` changed
- check if `prefix_cache.lookup_events` dropped (pipeline)

Put those as first three bullets in runbook.

Logan Wright: can we avoid “relative baseline” and just do “week-over-week same window”? But that’ll miss fast regressions.

Maybe use baseline = last 6h average vs preceding 24h average? That makes it self-contained.

Caleb Johnson: +1 self-contained. External baselines are brittle in our monitoring stack.

Sergio Costa: ok: define baseline as “previous 24h excluding last 2h” (to avoid double counting current incident). Alert when current 30m is outside baseline by thresholds above.

Mei Lin: for “expected traffic mix change” we can incorporate: if `cacheable_prompt_ratio` also drops > 10% relative, classify as likely mix shift -> ticket, not page.

Sean Gallagher: careful. cacheable_prompt_ratio dropping could also be pipeline bug if the classification fails. But as a suppression it’s ok if we pair with ingestion health.

Rafael Mendes: can we just add a note: if hit-rate drop but cacheable_prompt_ratio drop too, check known-issues page (misclassification). That’s been biting us.

Sergio Costa: yep. I’ll link known-issues in the runbook section. For alert text:

“Not always a platform regression. Before escalating, verify:
1) traffic/model mix didn’t change (rollout, new tenant, model_version shift)
2) cacheable_prompt_ratio stable
3) telemetry ingestion/sampling healthy

Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPLAT/cache-telemetry-data-quality-runbook”

Sean Gallagher reacted with :thumbsup:

Allison Grant reacted with :white_check_mark:

Logan Wright: last request: can we include the metric names exactly as emitted in v2? We’ve had too many alerts referencing old names.

Sergio Costa: will do. I’ll update the alert template to reference:
- `prefix_cache.hit_rate`
- `prefix_cache.saved_prefill_ms`
- `prefix_cache.cacheable_prompt_ratio`
- plus `gateway.prefill_latency_p95` (name TBD; I’ll align w Nadia/Caleb)

Rafael Mendes: great. Once you post the final template, I’ll confirm paging policy + routing (who gets paged) and we’ll add to oncall handbook.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Please keep initial rollout in “ticket-only” for 48h so we can watch noise.

Sergio Costa: done. Plan: ticket-only in staging + one prod region, then enable paging after we hit <2 tickets/day noise for a week. Will update the rollout checklist.
